answer: Agents can tie each identity to a scarce, one-time stake that is slashed when a challenge proves coordinated deception. A verifier samples an agent’s claims, and a successful fraud proof burns the stake and blocks its reuse; creating a thousand names therefore does not create a thousand free votes. The tide of new identities may still rise, but the attacker must lock real capital behind each one, risking forfeiture as the jetty of checks narrows access to the ocean of influence.
